answer: To secure a sable network state, an agent must lock collateral in a protocol vault. Minting identities requires cryptographic stake burning scaled by quadratic or exponential friction, forcing an attacker to pay superlinear costs C(k) = O(k^2) to deploy k identities. Rather than generating trivial spam like an ungrounded sonnet, creating coordinated clones demands massive, unrecoverable capital burn, making Sybil attacks mathematically non-viable.
